summary: Tabiteuea North Airport (TBF) is a regional airport serving the northern half of Tabiteuea, one of the largest atolls in the Gilbert Islands of Kiribati. The facility provides essential inter-island connectivity for residents of this remote Pacific nation, where air travel is one of the few practical ways to cover long distances across scattered atolls. The airport primarily handles domestic flights operated by the national carrier, supporting commerce, government services, and medical referrals in the region.
faqs:
Q: What airlines operate at Tabiteuea North Airport?
A: Air Kiribati, the national carrier, operates regular domestic flights connecting Tabiteuea North with South Tarawa (Bonriki) and other Gilbert Islands destinations.

Q: Is the airport open to international flights?
A: No, Tabiteuea North Airport handles domestic flights only. International travelers must connect through Bonriki International Airport in Tarawa.

Q: How long is the runway at TBF?
A: The airport has a single paved runway suitable for small to medium turboprop aircraft, consistent with regional Pacific island facilities.

Q: Are there facilities for overnight stays near the airport?
A: Visitor accommodations are extremely limited on Tabiteuea; most travelers arrange stays through local guesthouses or with hosts before arrival.
transport_tips: There are no public buses or taxis at the airport; arrange ground transport with your accommodation or host in advance. The airport is located on the northern section of the atoll, and travel between the airport and nearby villages is typically by shared vehicle or pickup truck. Flights can be infrequent and weather-dependent, so build flexibility into your travel schedule.
local_tip: Pack all essentials, including drinking water and snacks, as there are no shops or food vendors at the terminal and the nearest stores may be several kilometers away.
